description:
Single biggest UX lever from the review. Upstream pi-mono ships
a meaty system prompt (see
`tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts`
and referenced prompt files under `prompts/`) that primes the
model on:

  * the tool surface (what each tool does, when to use it)
  * expected output conventions (don't mention tools by name,
    don't ask permission, be proactive)
  * file-handling etiquette (read before edit, don't fabricate
    paths)
  * abort / cancel handling
  * code style guidelines (match existing, minimal diffs)

The real-world test runs with our Sonnet/Opus defaults show
the model is tool-*aware* but tentative without this prompt —
says things like "I can help you with Bash commands" instead
of just running `ls`.

Scope:
- Port `system-prompt.ts` as an Elixir module
  `OctoPi.Coder.SystemPrompt` that takes `{cwd, tools, ...}` and
  returns the rendered string.
- Mirror the prompt templates under `prompts/` as @external_
  resource bindings or a compile-time build step.
- Print / RPC / Interactive modes all default `:system_prompt`
  to this rendered string (unless explicitly overridden).

TDD:
- `SystemPrompt.render/1` with default opts produces a known-
  shape prompt (snapshot test — check specific substrings).
- Cwd interpolation works.
- Tool list interpolation works.
- An end-to-end Interactive run against FakeTransport verifies
  the system_prompt reaches the agent context.

Upstream test: check if there's a prompt snapshot test in
`tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/test/`. If yes, mirror it.
title: Port upstream system prompt for the coding agent
